name: John Singer Sargent
findings: Within his own canvases, rinnemann's green turns up as a small accent in 40% of the paintings that hold it, 3.4x the archive's rate (from 2080 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, toffee turns up as the lightest note in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 2.8x the archive's rate (from 2080 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, rhythm turns up as the shadow in 60% of the paintings that hold it, 3.2x the archive's rate (from 2080 paintings here).
Rarely uses dark olive brown, common in the same museum(s)' other paintings (from 2080 paintings here).
Pairs oxblood with rosewood more than chance would predict (4 of 2080 paintings here).
Pairs blackish grey with dim grey more than chance would predict (3 of 2080 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, black, raisin black) covers 65% of his paintings here.
Keeps 2 distinct palette families here, from smoky black, black to smoky black, dark olive brown.
